q: In the Notes app, which value should each note store in ownerId?
why: The uid never changes for an account and is not personal data; emails and names can change.

q: After a page reload, a signed-in user briefly sees the sign-in screen. Most likely cause?
o: The code reads auth.currentUser at start-up
why: currentUser is null until Auth restores the user. Decide the screen inside onAuthStateChanged.

q: A guest wrote notes with an anonymous account and now sets a password. What keeps the notes?
o: Create a new account and copy notes
why: Linking adds the new sign-in method to the same account, so the uid and all notes stay.

q: Your own server must know who is calling. What should the client send?
o: Its ID token, which the server verifies
why: Only a uid inside a token verified with the Admin SDK can be trusted; anyone can send a plain uid.

q: Every Google sign-in attempt fails with auth/operation-not-allowed. What do you check first?
o: Whether the Google provider is enabled
why: A provider that is not switched on in the console refuses every attempt.

q: You want SMS phone sign-in. What is the main risk to plan for?
o: Fake SMS traffic causing a large bill
It only works on the web
why: Each SMS is billed and attackers can trigger many; limit countries and set a budget alert.

q: Firebase Auth blocks users who have not verified their email.
why: Auth only reports emailVerified; your app (and your rules) decide what unverified users may do.

q: Leaving Firebase Auth later is possible but takes work: export users, handle the password hash format, and keep or remap uids.
why: auth:export gives the accounts, but the new system must accept the modified scrypt hashes or users must reset passwords.
